A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SKALD study, and all supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 retains the main paper and adds supplementary Sections 6–9 and Figures 7–9.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original benchmark evaluations and ablations. Section 4.5 reports an original 20-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and the user study, and adds qualitative assembly comparisons in Figures 7–9.

M1.justification: The LCA architecture, contrastive learning followed by regression, sequence-length decorrelation, beam search, and optional text scoring are unchanged. The supplement adds documentation without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multi-shot assembly on VSPD, MSV3C, and stock-footage user-study examples. The added pizza-making, kitchen-cleaning, and environmental-awareness illustrations use the existing assembly task without establishing new benchmark coverage or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 includes CLIP, Frozen-in-Time, Transcript-to-Video, and RATV; Table 2 includes Random, CLIP, Frozen-in-Time, and CLIP4Clip. Figures 7–9 extend the existing qualitative comparison with CLIP4Clip.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the splits, metrics, and training settings. However, new Section 6 describes 5,648 videos as the resulting MSV3C dataset, whereas the retained experimental split totals 2,850 videos. v1 placed 5,648 before further filtering. The PDFs do not reconcile these counts, leaving uncertainty about the intended sample pool; the additional procedural details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 8 and Figures 7–9 add three case studies examining visual and narrative continuity against CLIP4Clip. The existing beam-size, training-strategy, shot-replacement, and length-regularization ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 20 user-study participants and three rating sessions per pair. The supplement adds no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4, Figure 6's LCA scores, and the 45%/22%/33% user preferences are unchanged. Figures 7–9 add qualitative results supporting coherence advantages on three further examples, without new quantitative scores.

T1.justification: The problem definition, NCE and MSE objectives, combined visual/text score, SMS definition, and search-complexity analysis are unchanged. The supplement introduces no mathematical derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same methodological, annotation-efficiency, performance, and user-preference claims. The shortened conclusion preserves their meaning and the proposed future extension to longer videos.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains that the source dataset's scene cuts did not align accurately with shot transitions, motivating TransNetV2; v1 names the tool without this rationale. The principal interpretations of coherence, efficiency, and annotation requirements remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The supplement newly specifies lowest-variance-quartile filtering, random sampling of 3–12 consecutive shots, and exclusion of user-study submissions failing golden-pair controls. v2 also adds a project URL and names demo files. Their external availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 34 references and research positioning are retained. Supplementary citations reuse existing works; changed reference back-pointers reflect pagination rather than new literature.

P1.justification: v2 appends four supplementary sections, adds acknowledgements and a project-link sentence, lightly edits the Figure 2 caption, and condenses the conclusion. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: v2 adds three qualitative figures on a supplementary page while retaining Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–4. Other changes are limited caption edits and text reflow. Figure 9's environmental-awareness comparison has an incongruous sentence about cleaning tasks in its caption.

improvement.justification: The added filtering, sampling, and user-study control details improve reproducibility and transparency, while Figures 7–9 provide additional inspectable qualitative evidence. These are limited gains because the method and quantitative evidence remain unchanged. Unreconciled dataset totals and the erroneous cleaning-task sentence in Figure 9's caption temper the improvement.
